newsitem.title: DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC OF CONGO: Congo's Brazzaville calm as 72-hour truce starts.
newsitem.headline: Congo's Brazzaville calm as 72-hour truce starts.

text.p: Brazzaville was calm on Wednesday at the start of a three-day ceasefire between two militias who have fought for control of the Congolese capital since early June.
"It's all very quiet and has been all night," one Western security official said by telephone from the city.
"There has been one shot here, one shot there, but nothing serious and no comparison with before."
Other residents also said it was calm after the truce, brokered in talks at the French embassy, began at midnight (2300 GMT Tuesday).
No gunfire or artillery fire, usually clearly audible, could be heard across the Congo River in the twin city of Kinshasa, capital of the former Zaire, now renamed the Democratic Republic of Congo.

Forces loyal to President Pascal Lissouba and foes backing his rival, former military leader Denis Sassou Nguesso, have fought each other through the streets of the old French colonial capital since June 5.
The two men were seen as front-runners for presidential elections due at the end of July but both say the fighting has endangered plans to hold the poll.
